sections.heading: Mendelian Inheritance, Test Cross & Non-Mendelian Deviations
sections.summary: Gregor Mendel (1856-1863) analysed 7 contrasting traits in Pisum sativum across 14 true-breeding lines, establishing Dominance, Segregation, and Independent Assortment. Subsequent discoveries revealed incomplete dominance, co-dominance, multiple allelism, pleiotropy, and polygenic inheritance.
keyPoints: 7 Pea Traits (Dom vs Rec): Stem height (Tall/Dwarf), Flower colour (Violet/White), Flower position (Axial/Terminal), Pod shape (Inflated/Constricted), Pod colour (Green/Yellow), Seed shape (Round/Wrinkled — SBE1 starch branching enzyme retrotransposon insertion!), Seed colour (Yellow/Green).

Chromosomal locations in Pea (2n=14): Traits reside on only 4 chromosomes (1, 4, 5, 7); Seed colour & flower colour on Ch 1; Pod shape, stem height, flower position on Ch 4 (height & pod shape close!).
Test cross (F1 x Homozygous Recessive): Monohybrid = 1:1; Dihybrid = 1:1:1:1; determines unknown heterozygote vs homozygote dominant genotype.

Incomplete Dominance (Dog flower / Snapdragon Antirrhinum majus, Mirabilis jalapa): F1 pink; F2 phenotype AND genotype ratio BOTH = 1:2:1 (Red : Pink : White). Starch grain size in pea shows complete dominance for seed shape yet incomplete dominance for grain size!

Co-dominance & Multiple Alleles: Human ABO blood group (gene I has 3 alleles I^A, I^B, i in population -> 6 genotypes, 4 phenotypes; I^A & I^B are co-dominant expressing both sugars on RBC surface); AB blood group = I^A I^B.

Pleiotropy (1 gene -> multiple phenotypes: Phenylketonuria PAH defect -> mental retardation + reduced hair/skin pigmentation) vs Polygenic Inheritance (multiple genes -> continuous additive variation: Human skin colour 3 genes A, B, C -> bell curve; Wheat kernel colour).

sections.heading: Chromosomal Theory, Linkage (Morgan), Sex Determination & Mutations
sections.summary: Sutton and Boveri (1902) united Mendel's factors with chromosome behaviour, experimentally verified by T.H. Morgan using Drosophila melanogaster (2-week life cycle, single mating yields hundreds, clear sexual dimorphism). Linkage strength inversely tracks physical gene distance.
keyPoints: T.H. Morgan Drosophila dihybrid X-linked crosses: Cross A (yellow body & white eyes): 98.7% parental, ONLY 1.3% recombinant (tight linkage!); Cross B (white eyes & miniature wing): 62.8% parental, 37.2% recombinant (loose linkage!).
Alfred Sturtevant used recombination frequencies (% recombination = 1 centiMorgan / map unit) to construct the first genetic chromosome maps.

Sex Determination Systems: (1) XX-XY Male Heterogamety (Humans, Drosophila); (2) XX-XO Male Heterogamety (Grasshopper — Henking discovered X-body 1891); (3) ZZ-ZW Female Heterogamety (Birds, Reptiles, Fishes — female determines chick sex!); (4) Haplodiploidy (Honeybee: Female 2n=32 from fertilised egg; Male drone n=16 parthenogenetic, NO father & NO sons, has grandfather & grandsons!).

Mutations: Point mutation (single base pair change, e.g., Sickle-cell anaemia GAG -> GUG) vs Frameshift insertion/deletion (insertion/deletion of 1 or 2 bases shifts entire reading frame; 3 bases inserts/deletes 1 intact amino acid without frameshift).
Environmental sex determination examples outside humans: Temperature-dependent sex determination in certain reptiles (turtles/crocodiles) vs genetic XX-XY/ZZ-ZW mechanisms.

sections.heading: Pedigree Analysis, Mendelian Disorders & Chromosomal Syndromes
sections.summary: Human pedigree charts trace inheritance patterns across generations using standard symbols (filled = affected, half-filled/dot = carrier, diamond = unspecified sex, double line = consanguineous marriage). Distinguish autosomal vs X-linked and dominant vs recessive disorders cleanly.
keyPoints: Autosomal Recessive (Sickle-cell, PKU, Thalassemia, Cystic fibrosis): Skips generations; unaffected carrier parents can have affected daughters or sons (1/4 probability). Sickle-cell anaemia: single base substitution GAG -> GUG at 6th codon of beta-globin (chromosome 11) substitutes Glutamic acid (polar) -> Valine (hydrophobic); Hb^A Hb^S carriers enjoy malaria protection!

Thalassemia (quantitative globin reduction vs sickle-cell qualitative defect): Alpha-thalassemia (2 closely linked genes HBA1, HBA2 on Ch 16 -> 4 alleles); Beta-thalassemia (single gene HBB on Ch 11); Phenylketonuria (lack Phenylalanine hydroxylase -> phenylpyruvic acid excreted in urine).

X-Linked Recessive (Haemophilia, Red-green Colour Blindness ~8% males vs 0.4% females): Criss-cross inheritance (mother -> son -> granddaughter); NEVER passes directly from father to son; Haemophilia B (Queen Victoria pedigree) rarely affects females (requires carrier mother + haemophilic father).
Autosomal Dominant (Myotonic dystrophy): Does NOT skip generations; every affected child has at least one affected parent.

Chromosomal Aneuploidy (non-disjunction during meiosis/mitosis) & Polyploidy (cytokinesis failure in plants): Down's Syndrome (Trisomy 21, 47 chromosomes, Langdon Down 1866: short stature, small round head, furrowed tongue, partially open mouth, palm crease, congenital heart & mental retardation).

Sex-Chromosome Aneuploidy: Klinefelter's Syndrome (47, XXY: tall sterile male, masculine overall with feminine breast development GYNAECOMASTIA) vs Turner's Syndrome (45, X0: sterile female, rudimentary ovaries, lack secondary sexual characters, webbed neck).

sections.heading: DNA Search, Double Helix Packaging & Semi-Conservative Replication
sections.summary: Experiments by Griffith, Avery-MacLeod-McCarty, and Hershey-Chase conclusively proved DNA is the universal genetic material (except RNA viruses). Eukaryotic DNA (~2.2 m long in 6.6 x 10^9 bp diploid human cell) coils around basic octamer histones into nucleosomes and replicates semi-conservatively.
keyPoints: Genetic Material Proofs: Frederick Griffith (1928, Streptococcus pneumoniae S-virulent smooth capsule vs R-rough non-virulent) discovered Transforming Principle; Avery, MacLeod & McCarty (1944) proved ONLY DNase destroyed transformation (proteases & RNase did not); Hershey & Chase (1952, T2 phage + E. coli) used radioactive 35S (protein coat stayed in supernatant) & 32P (DNA entered bacterial pellet) for unequivocal proof!

DNA vs RNA stability: 2'-OH group on ribose makes RNA reactive/labile and catalytic; DNA has 2'-deoxyribose + Thymine (5-methyl uracil) conferring superior chemical stability; RNA mutates faster (better for short-lived viruses, worse for genome storage).

B-DNA Watson-Crick parameters (Chargaff A=T, G=C; Purines = Pyrimidines): Right-handed helix, diameter 2.0 nm (20 A), pitch 3.4 nm (10 bp/turn), axial rise 0.34 nm; A=T (2 H-bonds), G===C (3 H-bonds); antiparallel polarity 5'->3' and 3'->5'.

Chromatin Packaging: Positively charged basic proteins HISTONES (rich in Lysine & Arginine) form 8-subunit Histone Octamer (H2A, H2B, H3, H4 x 2) wrapped by ~200 bp negatively charged DNA -> NUCLEOSOME (sealed by H1 linker); Euchromatin (loosely packed, transcriptionally active, light stain) vs Heterochromatin (dense, inactive, dark stain).

Semi-Conservative Replication: Meselson & Stahl (1958, E. coli in 15NH4Cl -> 14NH4Cl: 20 min Gen I = 100% hybrid; 40 min Gen II = 50% hybrid + 50% light); Taylor (1958) proved same in eukaryotic Vicia faba roots using 3H-thymidine.

Replication Machinery: Ori site; Helicase unwinds fork; DNA-dependent DNA Polymerase III catalyses polymerisation ONLY in 5'->3' direction using dNTPs (dual role: substrate + energy via 2 terminal phosphates!); Leading strand (continuous on 3'->5' template) vs Lagging strand (discontinuous Okazaki fragments on 5'->3' template joined by DNA Ligase); RNA primer synthesised by Primase.

sections.heading: Transcription, RNA Processing & Genetic Code
sections.summary: Transcription copies one DNA template strand (3'->5') into RNA using RNA Polymerase without needing a primer. Eukaryotes segregate three nuclear RNA polymerases and process monocistronic hnRNA via capping, intron splicing, and poly-A tailing before cytoplasmic translation.
keyPoints: Transcription Unit: Promoter (upstream 5' end of coding strand), Structural Gene, Terminator (downstream 3' end). Template strand (3'->5') is transcribed; Coding strand (5'->3') matches the RNA sequence EXCEPT Thymine replaces Uracil!
Prokaryotes: Monocistronic? NO — Polycistronic structural genes, coupled transcription-translation in cytosol, SINGLE RNA Polymerase binds Sigma factor (initiation) and Rho factor (termination).

Eukaryotes (split genes: Exons expressed + Introns intervening): RNA Pol I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, 5.8S); RNA Pol II transcribes hnRNA (precursor of mRNA); RNA Pol III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNAs.

Post-transcriptional processing (Nucleus): (1) Capping (methyl guanosine triphosphate added at 5' end), (2) Splicing (spliceosomes remove non-coding introns and join exons — remnant of ancient RNA world!), (3) Tailing (200-300 adenylate residues added template-independently at 3' end).

Genetic Code (Marshall Nirenberg cell-free synthesis, Har Gobind Khorana homopolymers/copolymers, Severo Ochoa enzyme PNPase template-independent RNA synthesis): 64 triplet codons = 61 sense + 3 Stop/Nonsense (UAA, UAG, UGA); AUG = Dual role (Start codon + Methionine); Degenerate (same amino acid coded by >1 codon), Unambiguous/Specific, Commaless, Nearly Universal (minor mitochondrial/protozoan exceptions).

sections.heading: Translation, Lac Operon, Human Genome Project & DNA Fingerprinting
sections.summary: Ribosomes translate mRNA 5'->3' using aminoacyl-tRNA adapters (Cloverleaf 2D / Inverted-L 3D). Prokaryotic gene expression responds rapidly via the inducible negative Lac Operon, while HGP and VNTR DNA fingerprinting revolutionised genomics and forensics.
keyPoints: Translation steps: Charging/Aminoacylation of tRNA (ATP + amino acid -> aminoacyl-tRNA); Initiation at 5' UTR + AUG; Elongation (23S rRNA in bacteria = RIBOZYME peptidyl transferase forming peptide bond!); Termination when release factor binds UAA/UAG/UGA.

Lac Operon (Francois Jacob & Jacque Monod): Polycistronic structural genes z (beta-galactosidase: lactose -> glucose + galactose), y (permease: increases cell permeability to beta-galactosides), a (transacetylase); Regulator gene i constitutively synthesises Repressor protein.

Lac Operon control: Strictly NEGATIVE regulation (and positive via cAMP-CAP); Absence of lactose -> active repressor binds Operator (o) blocking RNA Polymerase -> OFF; Presence of ALLOLACTOSE/lactose (actual inducer!) binds & inactivates repressor -> Operator free -> ON!

Human Genome Project (1990-2003, Mega Project ~3 x 10^9 bp, ~30,000 genes, avg gene 3000 bp, Dystrophin largest gene = 2.4 million bp): Less than 2% genome codes for proteins; Chromosome 1 has most genes (2968), Chromosome Y has fewest (231); ~1.4 million SNPs; Sequenced model organisms include Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila, Arabidopsis, Rice; BAC & YAC vectors.

DNA Fingerprinting (Alec Jeffreys, VNTR minisatellites 0.1-20 kb repeating tandemly in satellite DNA): Isolation -> Restriction digestion -> Gel Electrophoresis -> Southern Blotting onto nitrocellulose/nylon membrane -> Hybridisation with radioactive VNTR probe -> Autoradiography. Identical ONLY in monozygotic twins!

solvedExamples.question: E. coli grown completely in 15N heavy medium is shifted to 14N light medium and allowed to replicate for 80 minutes (generation time = 20 min). Find the percentage of Hybrid (15N/14N) and Light (14N/14N) DNA molecules.
steps: Number of generations n = 80 / 20 = 4 generations -> total DNA molecules = 2^4 = 16.

solvedExamples.question: Given a DNA template strand sequence: 3'-A T G C A T G G A T T A-5', write the complementary mRNA sequence, identify the number of amino acids coded, and give the coding strand sequence.
steps: Transcribe 3'->5' template into 5'->3' mRNA (A->U, T->A, G->C, C->G): 5'-U A C G U A C C U A A U-3'. Wait — check stop codons! Codons: UAC (Tyr) - GUA (Val) - CCU (Pro) - AAU (Asn) -> 4 codons, zero stop codons.
Wait: if template were 3'-T A C A T T-5', mRNA = 5'-A U G U A A-3' (AUG = 1 amino acid, UAA = stop).
For the given template 3'-A T G C A T G G A T T A-5': mRNA = 5'-U A C G U A C C U A A U-3' (4 codons -> 4 amino acids if translated in frame); Coding DNA strand = 5'-T A C G T A C C T A A T-3'.

sections.heading: Population Attributes, Density & Age Pyramids
sections.summary: Ecology bridges organismal adaptation with population, community, ecosystem, and biome dynamics. A population possesses group-level attributes — birth/death rates, sex ratio, age distribution, and density — that an individual organism lacks.
keyPoints: Per-capita rates: Birth rate = births / initial population (e.g., 8 new lotus plants added to 20 -> 8/20 = 0.4 offspring/lotus/year); Death rate = deaths / initial population (4 fruitflies die out of 40 -> 0.1 deaths/fly/week).

Age Pyramids (pre-reproductive base, reproductive middle, post-reproductive top): Triangular / Broad base = EXPANDING population; Bell-shaped = STABLE population; Urn-shaped / Narrow base = DECLINING population.

Population Density (N) measurement: Biomass / % cover (better than count for huge banyan tree vs 200 Parthenium!), Relative density (fish caught per trap), Indirect pug marks & faecal pellets (tiger census!).

Four basic density processes: Natality (B) and Immigration (I) INCREASE N; Mortality (D) and Emigration (E) DECREASE N -> N_(t+1) = N_t + [(B + I) - (D + E)]. Under normal conditions B & D dominate; in a newly colonised habitat, Immigration (I) dominates!
Sex ratio: Expressed as percentage of females vs males (e.g., 60% females and 40% males in a given population — an attribute only of a population, never an individual).

sections.heading: Population Growth Models & Life History Variation
sections.summary: Populations grow exponentially (J-curve) only when resources are unlimited, whereas real-world environmental resistance enforces a carrying capacity K yielding the S-shaped Verhulst-Pearl logistic curve.
keyPoints: Exponential (Geometric) Growth: dN/dt = (b - d) N = r N; Integral form N_t = N_0 * e^(rt), producing a J-shaped curve (r = intrinsic rate of natural increase; Norway rat r=0.015, Flour beetle r=0.12, Human India 1981 r=0.0205).
Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth: dN/dt = rN * ((K - N) / K), where K = Carrying Capacity (nature's max sustainable limit) and (K - N)/K = environmental resistance.
Logistic phases: Lag phase (slow) -> Acceleration phase -> Deceleration phase -> Asymptote (when N = K, dN/dt = 0); Maximum growth rate occurs at inflexion point N = K / 2!

Life History Strategies (maximising Darwinian fitness / r-value): Breed ONCE in lifetime (Pacific salmon fish, Bamboo) vs breed MANY times (most birds, mammals); Produce huge number of small offspring (Oysters, Pelagic fishes) vs small number of large offspring (Birds, Mammals).
Realistic growth constraint: Because environmental resources (food, space) are finite for most animal populations, the logistic growth model is far more realistic than unchecked exponential growth.

sections.heading: Population Interactions: Mutualism, Competition, Predation & Parasitism
sections.summary: No species survives in isolation; interspecific interactions govern food webs, co-evolution, and niche partitioning. NCERT tests exact interaction signs (+, -, 0) and organism pairings.
keyPoints: Predation (+ / -): Transfers energy across trophic levels, keeps prey populations under control (Prickly pear cactus in Australia checked by Cactoblastis moth!), maintains species diversity (Pisaster starfish removal caused >10 invertebrate extinctions!). Prey defences: Camouflage, Monarch butterfly distastefulness (accumulated from poisonous milkweed caterpillar!), Acacia thorns & Calotropis cardiac glycosides!

Competition (- / -): Unrelated species can compete (flamingos & resident fish for zooplankton); Interference competition (Abingdon tortoise extinct on Galapagos within decade after goats introduced); Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle (2 closely related species competing for SAME limiting resource cannot coexist indefinitely); Connell's elegant field experiment (Balanus barnacle excludes smaller Chathamalus); MacArthur's 5 warbler species coexist via RESOURCE PARTITIONING (different foraging times/canopy zones!).

Parasitism (+ / -): Host-specific co-evolution (loss of unnecessary sense organs, suckers/hooks, loss of digestive system, high reproductive capacity); Ectoparasites (Lice, Ticks, Copepods on marine fish, Cuscuta total stem parasite without chlorophyll) vs Endoparasites (Liver fluke Fasciola needing 2 intermediate hosts snail & fish; Plasmodium); Brood Parasitism (Koel/Cuckoo lays eggs resembling host Crow's eggs!).
Commensalism (+ / 0): Orchid epiphyte on Mango branch, Barnacles on Whale back, Cattle Egret & grazing cattle (insects flushed out), Sea Anemone (stinging tentacles) & Clownfish.

Mutualism (+ / +): Lichens (algae + fungus), Mycorrhiza (fungi + higher plant roots absorbing phosphorus), Fig tree & Wasp (strict 1-to-1 obligate co-evolution: wasp pollinates while laying eggs inside developing fruits/ovules), Mediterranean Orchid Ophrys & Colpa bumblebee (PSEUDOCOPULATION — petal mimics female bee's size, colour & markings -> SEXUAL DECEIT!).
Amensalism (- / 0): Penicillium notatum secreting penicillin inhibits Staphylococcus bacteria while remaining unaffected; Juglans (walnut) juglone.

sections.heading: Ecosystem Structure, Productivity & Decomposition
sections.summary: An ecosystem functions as a self-sustaining structural unit with vertical stratification and four functional pillars: productivity, decomposition, energy flow, and nutrient cycling. Solar energy capture fixes carbon into GPP and usable NPP, while detritivores and decomposers mineralise dead organic matter.
keyPoints: Stratification: Vertical distribution of species at different levels (e.g., Trees top -> Shrubs second -> Herbs/Grasses bottom in forest).

Primary Productivity: Gross Primary Productivity (GPP = total organic matter rate during photosynthesis) minus Respiratory losses (R) = Net Primary Productivity (NPP = GPP - R, biomass available to heterotrophs!).

Global Biosphere NPP = ~170 billion tons (dry weight) annually; despite covering >70% Earth surface, OCEANS contribute ONLY 55 billion tons (low nutrient N/light limitation); rest 115 billion tons comes from land!
Secondary Productivity: Rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.

Decomposition (Detritus = dead plant/animal remains + faecal matter; requires O2 & warm moist climate; slowed by lignin/chitin, low temp & anaerobiosis, accelerated by N & water-soluble sugars): 5 sequential steps — (1) Fragmentation (detritivores like earthworm break detritus), (2) Leaching (water-soluble inorganic nutrients seep down & precipitate as unavailable salts), (3) Catabolism (bacterial/fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances), (4) Humification (dark amorphous colloidal HUMUS resists microbial action, decomposes slowly, nutrient reservoir), (5) Mineralisation (microbes degrade humus releasing inorganic nutrients).

sections.heading: Energy Flow, Food Chains & Ecological Pyramids
sections.summary: Except for deep-sea hydrothermal ecosystems, the Sun is the sole energy source driving unidirectional trophic transfer obeying the Second Law of Thermodynamics. Ecological pyramids graph number, biomass, and energy across trophic levels, revealing key aquatic and tree exceptions.
keyPoints: Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR): <50% of incident solar radiation is PAR; plants capture ONLY 2-10% of PAR (or ~1-5% of total incident solar radiation)!
Food Chains: Grazing Food Chain (GFC: Grass -> Goat -> Man; major conduit in AQUATIC ecosystems) vs Detritus Food Chain (DFC: Dead matter -> Decomposers; major conduit in TERRESTRIAL ecosystems!).
Lindeman's 10% Law: Only ~10% of energy is transferred to each successive trophic level; 90% is lost as heat/respiration — restricting food chains to 3-4 trophic levels.
Pyramid of Number: Upright in Grassland (Producers > Herbivores > Carnivores); INVERTED or Spindle-shaped in a Single Tree ecosystem (1 tree -> many insects -> fewer/many birds/hyperparasites).

Pyramid of Biomass: Upright in Forest/Grassland; INVERTED in Sea/Aquatic ecosystems (small standing crop of rapidly reproducing phytoplankton supports much larger standing crop of zooplankton & fishes!).

Pyramid of Energy: ALWAYS UPRIGHT (never inverted!) because energy is lost as heat at every trophic transfer; Limitations of pyramids: exclude same species at multiple levels (e.g., Sparrow = T2 seeds + T3 insects), assume simple food chains, and omit SAPROPHYTES/decomposers!

sections.heading: Biodiversity Patterns, Loss ('Evil Quartet') & Conservation
sections.summary: Edward Wilson popularised the term 'Biodiversity' across genetic, species, and ecological levels. India holds 2.4% of world land area yet contributes an impressive 8.1% of global species diversity, facing severe loss driven by the Evil Quartet.
keyPoints: Three Biodiversity Levels: Genetic (Rauwolfia vomitoria potency/reserpine variation in Himalayas; >50,000 Rice strains & 1,000 Mango varieties in India), Species (Western Ghats > Eastern Ghats amphibian diversity), Ecological (deserts, rainforests, mangroves, coral reefs).

Global Estimates: IUCN (2004) >1.5 million described; Robert May conservative estimate = ~7 million total species (>70% animals, 70% of animals = Insects; Fungi species > Fishes+Amphibians+Reptiles+Mammals combined!).

Latitudinal Gradients & Species-Area Relationship: Diversity peaks in Tropics (23.5 deg N to 23.5 deg S — Columbia 1400 birds, Amazon rainforest >40,000 plants, 1,25,000 invertebrates; long undisturbed evolutionary time, constant climate, more solar energy). Alexander von Humboldt: S = C A^Z (log S = log C + Z log A; Z = 0.1-0.2 normally, 0.6-1.2 for continents, 1.15 for tropical frugivorous birds/mammals!).

David Tilman's plot experiments (more species -> less year-to-year biomass fluctuation, higher productivity) & Paul Ehrlich's Rivet Popper Hypothesis (Airplane = Ecosystem, Rivets = Species, Wing rivets = Keystones!).

Evil Quartet of Biodiversity Loss: (1) Habitat loss & fragmentation (MOST IMPORTANT — Tropical rainforests shrank from 14% to 6%; Amazon 'Lungs of the Planet' cleared for soyabeans/beef!), (2) Over-exploitation (Steller's sea cow, Passenger pigeon), (3) Alien species invasions (Nile perch wiped >200 Lake Victoria cichlid fishes; Parthenium, Lantana, Eichhornia; African catfish Clarias gariepinus!), (4) Co-extinctions (host fish-parasite, fig-wasp).

Conservation: Narrowly utilitarian, Broadly utilitarian (O2 20% from Amazon, pollination), Ethical; In-situ (Protected areas: 34 Global Hotspots covering <2% land yet cutting extinction ~30% — India has 3: Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, Himalaya; 14 Biosphere Reserves, 90 National Parks, 448 Wildlife Sanctuaries, Sacred Groves like Khasi/Jaintia Meghalaya, Aravalli) vs Ex-situ (Zoo, Botanical garden, Seed banks, Cryopreservation -196 deg C); Earth Summit Rio (1992) & World Summit Johannesburg (2002).

sections.heading: Basis of Classification & Lower Non-Chordates (Porifera to Platyhelminthes)
sections.summary: Animal Kingdom classifies phyla using organisation level, body symmetry, germ layers, coelom, segmentation, and notochord. Early metazoans span cellular sponges through diploblastic cnidarians/ctenophores to acoelomate flatworms.
keyPoints: Organisation & Symmetry: Cellular (Porifera, asymmetrical), Tissue (Coelenterata & Ctenophora, radial), Organ (Platyhelminthes, bilateral), Organ-system (Aschelminthes to Chordata; Adult Echinoderms show radial symmetry while their larvae are bilateral!).
Coelom: Acoelomate (Porifera to Platyhelminthes), Pseudocoelomate (ONLY Aschelminthes — mesoderm scattered in pouches!), Eucoelomate (Annelida to Chordata).

Porifera (Sponges — Sycon, Spongilla freshwater, Euspongia bath sponge): Water CANAL system (Ostia -> Spongocoel -> Osculum) lined by flagellated CHOANOCYTES (collar cells); spongin fibres / calcareous or siliceous spicules; intracellular digestion; hermaphrodite.

Coelenterata / Cnidaria (Physalia Portuguese man-of-war, Adamsia sea anemone, Pennatula sea-pen, Gorgonia sea-fan, Meandrina brain coral): Cnidoblasts/cnidocytes (nematocysts) for anchorage/defence/capture; gastro-vascular cavity with single hypostome opening; corals have CaCO3 skeleton; METAGENESIS in Obelia (asexual Polyp -> sexual Medusa -> Polyp; Aurelia is medusa, Hydra/Adamsia are polyps!).
Ctenophora (Sea walnuts / Comb jellies — Pleurobrachia, Ctenoplana): Exclusively marine, diploblastic, 8 external rows of ciliated COMB PLATES, marked BIOLUMINESCENCE, sexual reproduction ONLY.

Platyhelminthes (Flatworms — Taenia tapeworm, Fasciola liver fluke): Dorsoventrally flattened, bilateral, triploblastic acoelomate; hooks & suckers in parasites; FLAME CELLS for osmoregulation & excretion; Planaria exhibits high regeneration.

sections.heading: Higher Non-Chordates (Aschelminthes to Hemichordata)
sections.summary: Triploblastic organ-system invertebrates diversify from pseudocoelomate roundworms into true coelomate segmented annelids, jointed-appendage arthropods, soft-bodied molluscs, spiny-skinned echinoderms, and stomochord-bearing hemichordates.
keyPoints: Aschelminthes (Roundworms — Ascaris, Wuchereria filarial worm, Ancylostoma hookworm): Circular cross-section, complete alimentary canal with muscular pharynx, excretory tube with excretory pore, dioecious (females longer than males!).

Annelida (Nereis aquatic dioecious with parapodia, Pheretima, Hirudinaria blood-sucking leech monoecious): True METAMERIC segmentation, longitudinal & circular muscles, NEPHRIDIA (osmoregulation/excretion), paired ganglia + double ventral solid nerve cord.

Arthropoda (Largest phylum >2/3 named species!): Chitinous exoskeleton, head-thorax-abdomen, jointed appendages; Gills (prawn), Book gills (Limulus king crab living fossil!), Book lungs (scorpion/spider), Tracheal system (insects); Statocysts balance; MALPIGHIAN TUBULES excretion; Economically useful (Apis, Bombyx, Laccifer), Vectors (Anopheles, Culex, Aedes), Gregarious pest (Locusta).

Mollusca (2nd largest — Pila apple snail, Pinctada pearl oyster, Sepia cuttlefish, Loligo squid, Octopus devil fish, Aplysia sea-hare, Dentalium tusk shell, Chaetopleura chiton): Unsegmented calcareous shell, head + muscular foot + visceral hump; soft MANTLE forms mantle cavity housing feather-like gills (ctenidia); mouth has file-like rasping RADULA.

Echinodermata (Asterias starfish, Echinus sea urchin, Antedon sea lily, Cucumaria sea cucumber, Ophiura brittle star): Calcareous endoskeleton of ossicles, exclusively marine, WATER VASCULAR SYSTEM (locomotion, food capture/transport, respiration), complete digestive tract (ventral mouth, dorsal anus), NO excretory system!

Hemichordata (Balanoglossus, Saccoglossus): Worm-like marine animals formerly under Chordata; body = Proboscis + Collar + Trunk; rudimentary STOMOCHORD in collar (NOT true notochord!); proboscis gland excretion; gill-slit respiration.

sections.heading: Phylum Chordata: Protochordates & Vertebrata Classes
sections.summary: All chordates share a dorsal hollow single nerve cord, notochord, paired pharyngeal gill slits, post-anal tail, and ventral heart at some life stage. Vertebrata replaces the embryonic notochord with a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column.
keyPoints: Protochordates (exclusively marine): Urochordata / Tunicata (Ascidia, Salpa, Doliolum — notochord ONLY in larval tail!) vs Cephalochordata (Branchiostoma / Amphioxus / Lancelet — notochord persists head-to-tail throughout life!).

Cyclostomata (Petromyzon lamprey, Myxine hagfish): Ectoparasites on fishes, 6-15 pairs gill slits, sucking circular mouth WITHOUT jaws, devoid of scales & paired fins, cartilaginous cranium; migrate to freshwater for spawning then die (ammocoete larva returns to ocean).

Chondrichthyes (Scoliodon dogfish, Pristis sawfish, Carcharodon great white shark, Trygon sting ray, Torpedo electric ray): Cartilaginous endoskeleton, ventral mouth, persistent notochord, PLACOID scales (backward-directed modified teeth!), gill slits WITHOUT operculum, NO air bladder -> MUST swim constantly to avoid sinking! Internal fertilisation (male pelvic CLASPERS), mostly viviparous.

Osteichthyes (Marine: Exocoetus flying fish, Hippocampus sea horse; Freshwater: Labeo rohu, Catla, Clarias magur; Aquarium: Betta, Pterophyllum): Bony endoskeleton, terminal mouth, 4 pairs gills covered by OPERCULUM, cycloid/ctenoid scales, AIR BLADDER for buoyancy, external fertilisation, mostly oviparous.

Amphibia (Bufo, Rana, Hyla, Salamandra, Ichthyophis limbless): Moist scaleless skin, tympanum ear, cloaca, 3-chambered heart, cold-blooded (poikilothermous). Reptilia (Chelone, Testudo, Chameleon, Calotes, Crocodilus 4-chambered heart!, Alligator, Naja, Bangarus, Vipera): Dry cornified epidermal scales/scutes, mostly 3-chambered heart (4 in crocodile!).

Aves (Corvus, Columba, Psittacula, Struthio flightless, Pavo, Aptenodytes penguin, Neophron vulture): Feathers, oil gland ONLY at tail base, PNEUMATIC hollow bones, Crop & Gizzard, air sacs supplementing lungs, 4-chambered heart, warm-blooded (homoiothermous). Mammalia (Oviparous Ornithorhynchus platypus; Marsupial Macropus kangaroo; Viviparous Pteropus, Camelus, Balaenoptera blue whale, Delphinus): Mammary glands, hair, pinnae, heterodont thecodont dentition, muscular diaphragm, 7 cervical vertebrae.

sections.heading: Animal Tissues: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular & Neural
sections.summary: Multicellular animals coordinate four primary tissues: Epithelial (lining/glands with specialised cell junctions), Connective (linking/supporting via collagen/elastin matrix), Muscular (contractile fibres), and Neural (excitable neurons + supporting neuroglia >50% volume).
keyPoints: Simple Epithelium: Squamous (thin irregular boundary — blood vessel walls & lung alveoli for diffusion), Cuboidal (ducts of glands & nephron tubules; PCT has microvilli brush border), Columnar (stomach & intestine lining, microvilli), Ciliated (bronchioles & fallopian tubes moving mucus/ovum!), Compound stratified epithelium (skin, buccal cavity, pharynx, pancreatic/salivary ducts — protection against chemical/mechanical stress).

Cell Junctions (in epithelium): TIGHT junctions (stop leaking across tissue), ADHERING junctions (cement neighbouring cells), GAP junctions (rapid communication via cytoplasm-connecting ion/small-molecule channels).

Glands: Unicellular (Goblet cells of alimentary canal) vs Multicellular (Salivary gland); Exocrine (ducts: mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, enzymes) vs Endocrine (ductless -> hormones directly into fluid bathing gland).

Connective Tissue (fibres secreted by fibroblasts except BLOOD!): Loose (Areolar beneath skin with fibroblasts/macrophages/mast cells; Adipose fat storage), Dense Regular (Tendon bone-to-muscle; Ligament bone-to-bone) vs Dense Irregular (skin), Specialised: Cartilage (solid pliable matrix resists compression, CHONDROCYTES in lacunae; nose tip, outer ear, intervertebral joints), Bone (hard non-pliable Ca-salt/collagen matrix, OSTEOCYTES in lacunae, Haversian canal lamellae), Blood (fluid plasma + RBC/WBC/platelets).

Muscle Fibres: Skeletal (striated, multinucleated, cylindrical, unbranched, voluntary), Smooth (fusiform/spindle unstriated, uninucleate, involuntary — blood vessels, stomach, intestine), Cardiac (striated, branched, uninucleate, involuntary, INTERCALATED DISCS = communication junctions allowing simultaneous contraction!).

sections.heading: Cockroach (Periplaneta americana): Complete Morphology & Anatomy
sections.summary: NMC retained Periplaneta americana (brown/black nocturnal omnivore, Class Insecta, 34-53 mm long). Its body divides into head, thorax, and abdomen covered by chitinous exoskeleton plates (sclerites) joined by flexible arthrodial membranes.
keyPoints: Exoskeleton & Head: Dorsal tergites + ventral sternites joined by thin arthrodial membrane; Head triangular at 90 deg right-angle to longitudinal axis (hypognathous, formed by fusion of 6 segments), biting-chewing mouthparts (labrum, 2 mandibles, 2 maxillae, labium, median flexible tongue HYPOPHARYNX).

Thorax & Wings/Legs: Prothorax + Mesothorax (forewings = opaque leathery TEGMINA covering hindwings at rest) + Metathorax (transparent membranous hindwings used in flight); 3 pairs walking legs; 10-segmented Abdomen (7th boat-shaped sternum + 8th + 9th form brood/genital pouch in FEMALE; 9th & 10th terga + 9th sternum form genital pouch in MALE; BOTH sexes carry 10th-segment jointed ANAL CERCI, ONLY MALE has short thread-like ANAL STYLES on 9th sternum!).

Digestive System: Foregut (cuticle-lined: mouth -> pharynx -> oesophagus -> CROP food storage -> GIZZARD/proventriculus with outer circular muscles & 6 chitinous teeth for grinding!) -> Midgut/Mesenteron (6-8 blind HEPATIC/GASTRIC CAECAE at foregut-midgut junction!) -> Hindgut (ileum, colon, rectum; 100-150 thin yellow MALPIGHIAN TUBULES at midgut-hindgut junction excreting URIC ACID — uricotelic!).

Circulation & Respiration: Open blood vascular system; colourless HAEMOLYMPH (plasma + haemocytes, NO respiratory pigment) fills haemocoel; 13-chambered (funnel-shaped) mid-dorsal tubular heart with ostia aided by 12 pairs of ALARY muscles; Respiration via tracheal tubes branching into tracheoles opening via 10 pairs of lateral SPIRACLES regulated by sphincters.

Nervous & Sense Organs: Double ventral solid nerve cord with 3 thoracic + 6 abdominal ganglia; Supra-oesophageal ganglion (brain) in head supplies antennae & compound eyes; Each compound eye has ~2,000 hexagonal OMMATIDIA giving MOSAIC VISION (more sensitivity, less resolution, common at night).

Reproductive System: Male (testes 4th-6th segments -> vas deferens -> seminal vesicle -> ejaculatory duct; MUSHROOM/utricular gland at 6th-7th segments + phallic/conglobate gland; spermatophores); Female (2 ovaries 2nd-6th segments with 8 ovarioles each -> oviducts -> common oviduct/vagina -> genital chamber; spermatheca 6th segment + collaterial glands); Fertilised eggs encased in dark reddish-brown OOTHECA (14-16 eggs each; female makes 9-10 oothecae); Paurometabolous development (nymph moults 13 times; only penultimate nymph has wing pads!).

sections.heading: Frog (Rana tigrina): Complete Morphology & Anatomy
sections.summary: Indian bullfrog Rana tigrina (Class Amphibia) is poikilothermic, showing camouflage and summer aestivation / winter hibernation. NMC explicitly highlights its respiratory versatility, 3-chambered heart with portal systems, nucleated RBCs, mesonephric excretory-reproductive link, and metamorphosis.
keyPoints: External & Sexual Dimorphism: Moist smooth mucus-lubricated olive-green skin (dorsal dark spots, ventral pale yellow, NEVER drinks water — absorbs via skin!); head + trunk (NO neck or tail); eyes with NICTITATING membrane; tympanum; forelimbs (4 digits) + webbed hindlimbs (5 digits). MALE ONLY has sound-producing VOCAL SACS and a COPULATORY PAD on the FIRST digit of FORELIMBS!

Digestive System: Short alimentary canal (carnivore!) -> bilobed tongue captures prey -> oesophagus -> stomach (HCl + gastric juices) -> duodenum receives bile (fat emulsification) & pancreatic juice -> intestine (villi & microvilli) -> rectum -> cloaca.

Respiration (3 modes): (1) Cutaneous respiration (through moist vascular skin — exclusive mode in water and during hibernation/aestivation!), (2) Buccopharyngeal respiration (buccal cavity lining on land), (3) Pulmonary respiration (pair of pink elongated lungs; positive-pressure buccal pumping with nostrils).

Vascular System: Closed circulation; 3-chambered heart (2 atria + 1 ventricle) enclosed in pericardium; triangular SINUS VENOSUS receives venae cavae on dorsal right atrium; ventricle opens into CONUS ARTERIOSUS on ventral side; BOTH Hepatic Portal System (digestive tract -> liver) AND Renal Portal System (lower body -> kidneys) present! RBCs are OVAL, BICONVEX, and NUCLEATED containing Hb.

Excretion & Nervous Control: Ureotelic (excretes urea); pair of dark red bean-shaped MESONEPHRIC kidneys; 10 pairs of cranial nerves; Forebrain (olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres, unpaired diencephalon), Midbrain (paired OPTIC LOBES), Hindbrain (cerebellum + medulla oblongata -> spinal cord via foramen magnum).

Reproductive System: Male (yellowish ovoid testes attached to kidney upper part by MESORCHIUM peritoneum -> 10-12 VASA EFFERENTIA enter kidney opening into BIDDER'S CANAL -> collecting tubules -> urinogenital duct -> cloaca); Female (ovaries near kidneys with NO functional connection to kidneys! Oviducts open SEPARATELY from ureters into cloaca; lays 2,500-3,000 ova at a time; external fertilisation in water -> Tadpole larva).

derivationsAndGraphs.title: Frog Male Urinogenital Pathway vs Female Separate Ducts
derivationsAndGraphs.expressionOrCurve: Male Frog: Testis -> 10-12 Vasa Efferentia -> Bidder's Canal (inside Kidney) -> Urinogenital Duct (Ureter) -> Cloaca  |  Female: Ovary -> Ostium -> Oviduct -> Cloaca (Separate from Ureter)
derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Male frog ureter carries BOTH urine and sperms (urinogenital duct), whereas female frog ovaries have NO functional connection with kidneys and oviducts open separately.

derivationsAndGraphs.title: Cockroach Alimentary Canal & Junctional Landmarks
derivationsAndGraphs.expressionOrCurve: Mouth -> Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Crop -> Gizzard (6 teeth) --[6-8 Hepatic Caecae]--> Midgut --[100-150 Malpighian Tubules]--> Hindgut (Ileum -> Colon -> Rectum)
derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Hepatic caecae sit at the Foregut-Midgut junction (digestive juice); Malpighian tubules sit at the Midgut-Hindgut junction (uricotelic excretion).

derivationsAndGraphs.title: Chordate Evolutionary Ladder: Heart Chambers & RBC Nuclei
derivationsAndGraphs.expressionOrCurve: Pisces (2-ch single venous) -> Amphibia/Reptiles (3-ch incomplete double) -> Crocodile/Birds/Mammals (4-ch complete double)
derivationsAndGraphs.keyTakeaway: Frog RBCs are nucleated and oval, whereas mammalian RBCs (except camel/llama) are biconcave and enucleated.

comparison.title: Non-Chordate Phyla Diagnostic NCERT Matrix
rows: Muscular pharynx, Female longer than male

traps: Cockroach has a 13-chambered tubular heart with 12 pairs of alary muscles and 10 pairs of spiracles — NEVER mix up 10 spiracles with 13 heart chambers!
Cockroach Anal CERCI (10th segment) are present in BOTH males and females, whereas Anal STYLES (9th sternum) occur EXCLUSIVELY in MALE cockroaches!
Male Frog's copulatory pad sits on the FIRST digit of the FORELIMB (not hindlimb!), and Bidder's canal lies INSIDE the male kidney receiving 10-12 vasa efferentia.

Echinoderms have bilateral larvae yet radially symmetrical adults, and they completely LACK a specialised excretory system!

solvedExamples.question: Which set of animals correctly matches: (i) Pseudocoelomate, (ii) Bioluminescence, (iii) Living fossil arthropod, (iv) Flightless bird?
steps: Aschelminthes (e.g., Ascaris, Wuchereria) is the ONLY pseudocoelomate phylum.
Ctenophora (e.g., Pleurobrachia, Ctenoplana) is famous for bioluminescence.
Limulus (King crab) is the living fossil arthropod; Struthio (Ostrich) / Aptenodytes (Penguin) are flightless birds.
solvedExamples.answer: (i) Ascaris/Wuchereria, (ii) Pleurobrachia, (iii) Limulus, (iv) Struthio
solvedExamples.pitfall: Calling Platyhelminthes pseudocoelomate (they are acoelomate!) or confusing Limulus with Laccifer.

solvedExamples.question: Statement I: In female frogs, ovaries have a functional connection with the mesonephric kidneys via Bidder's canal. Statement II: Male frogs possess both vocal sacs and copulatory pads on the first digit of forelimbs.
steps: Check Statement I: Bidder's canal and vasa efferentia connecting testes to kidneys exist ONLY in MALE frogs; female ovaries have NO functional connection with kidneys -> Statement I is INCORRECT.
Check Statement II: Male frogs uniquely display sound-producing vocal sacs and copulatory pads on the 1st forelimb digit -> Statement II is CORRECT.
Match option: Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct.
solvedExamples.answer: Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
solvedExamples.pitfall: Assuming both sexes share Bidder's canal or placing the copulatory pad on the hindlimbs.

solvedExamples.question: A female Periplaneta americana produces 10 oothecae during her reproductive period, each containing 16 fertilised eggs. If 75% of emerging nymphs successfully complete all 13 moults to reach adulthood, how many adult cockroaches are formed?
steps: Total eggs across 10 oothecae = 10 x 16 = 160 fertilised eggs.
Calculate survivors: 75% survive through 13 paurometabolous nymphal moults -> 0.75 x 160.
Result = 120 adult cockroaches.
solvedExamples.answer: 120 adult cockroaches
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using 9-10 eggs per ootheca (9-10 is the number of oothecae laid; 14-16 is the number of eggs INSIDE each ootheca!).

solvedExamples.question: Match the Cockroach alimentary/excretory structures in the NCERT diagram: (1) Grinding food with 6 chitinous teeth, (2) Secreting digestive juice at foregut-midgut junction, (3) Removing nitrogenous waste at midgut-hindgut junction, (4) Storing food.
steps: (1) Proventriculus / Gizzard (6 chitinous teeth).
(2) 6-8 blind Hepatic/Gastric Caecae (foregut-midgut junction).
(3) 100-150 yellow Malpighian Tubules (midgut-hindgut junction).
(4) Sac-like Crop (food storage).
solvedExamples.answer: 1-Gizzard, 2-Hepatic caecae, 3-Malpighian tubules, 4-Crop
solvedExamples.pitfall: Reversing the junctions of Hepatic caecae (foregut-midgut) and Malpighian tubules (midgut-hindgut).

sections.heading: Chemical Analysis of Living Tissues & Elemental Composition
sections.summary: Grinding living tissue in trichloroacetic acid (Cl3CCOOH) separates low-molecular-weight acid-soluble filtrate (<800 Da) from the acid-insoluble retentate. Burning dry tissue produces ash containing inorganic elements (Ca2+, Mg2+, SO4^2-, PO4^3-).
keyPoints: Acid-soluble pool (~18-800 Da): Micromolecules (monosaccharides, amino acids, nucleotides, inorganic ions) roughly representing cytoplasmic composition.
Acid-insoluble fraction (Biomacromolecules >= 10,000 Da): Proteins, Nucleic acids, Polysaccharides PLUS Lipids (MW < 800 Da — an exception!).
Why Lipids appear in acid-insoluble pool: Lipids are NOT strictly polymeric macromolecules, yet cell & organelle membranes shatter into water-insoluble vesicles that cannot pass through cheesecloth!

NCERT Table 9.1 Earth Crust vs Human Body (% weight): Oxygen (46.6% vs 65.0%), Carbon (0.03% vs 18.5%), Nitrogen (very little vs 3.3%), Silicon (27.7% vs negligible!), Calcium (3.6% vs 1.5%), Hydrogen (0.14% vs 0.5%).
Average Composition of Cells (Table 9.4): Water (70-90%), Proteins (10-15%), Nucleic acids (5-7%), Carbohydrates (3%), Lipids (2%), Ions (1%).

sections.heading: Amino Acids, Zwitterions & Four Levels of Protein Structure
sections.summary: Amino acids are substituted methanes bearing an alpha-carbon attached to -H, -NH2, -COOH, and a variable -R group. Polypeptides fold hierarchically across four structural tiers, with Tertiary 3D conformation essential for enzymatic catalysis.
keyPoints: 20 proteinaceous amino acids: Glycine (R = -H; simplest, optically INACTIVE / no chiral carbon!), Alanine (R = -CH3), Serine (R = -CH2OH).

Functional categories: Acidic (Glutamic acid, Aspartic acid), Basic (Lysine, Arginine, Histidine), Neutral (Valine), Aromatic (Tyrosine, Phenylalanine, Tryptophan), Sulphur-containing (Cysteine, Methionine).
Zwitterion property: At isoelectric pH, amino acid exists as dipolar neutral zwitterion (+H3N-CHR-COO-); shifts to cation at low acidic pH and anion at high basic pH.

Protein structures: Primary (linear amino acid sequence; N-terminal left = 1st AA, C-terminal right = last AA); Secondary (right-handed alpha-helix or beta-pleated sheet stabilised by intramolecular/intermolecular H-bonds); Tertiary (hollow woollen ball 3D fold stabilised by disulphide -S-S-, H-bonds, ionic & hydrophobic bonds — MANDATORY for biological enzyme activity!); Quaternary (multiple polypeptide subunits: Adult Haemoglobin = 2 alpha + 2 beta = 4 subunits!).

Most abundant proteins: COLLAGEN (intercellular ground substance = most abundant protein in the ANIMAL world); RuBisCO (Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase = most abundant protein in the WHOLE BIOSPHERE!).

sections.heading: Carbohydrates (Polysaccharides) & Lipids
sections.summary: Polysaccharides are long chains of monosaccharides joined by glycosidic bonds (right end = reducing, left end = non-reducing). Lipids comprise water-insoluble fatty acids, glycerol esters, phospholipids, and sterols.
keyPoints: Homopolysaccharides: Cellulose (beta-1,4-glucose linear unbranched, NO complex helices -> does NOT hold I2 -> NO blue colour; plant cell wall, paper, cotton!); Starch (alpha-1,4 amylose helical + amylopectin -> traps I2 giving BLUE colour!); Glycogen (animal branched energy reserve).

Special polysaccharides: Inulin (polymer of FRUCTOSE — never confuse with peptide hormone Insulin!); Chitin (complex homopolysaccharide of N-acetylglucosamine NAG in arthropod exoskeleton & fungal cell walls).
Fatty acids: R-COOH where R = 1 to 19 carbons; Palmitic acid = 16 carbons (incl. carboxyl C, saturated); Arachidonic acid = 20 carbons (incl. carboxyl C, polyunsaturated with 4 double bonds!).

Simple lipids: Glycerol (trihydroxypropane) + 1/2/3 fatty acids -> monoglycerides, diglycerides, triglycerides via ester bonds; Fats (higher melting point, solid at room temp) vs Oils (gingelly oil, lower melting point, liquid!).
Compound & Derived lipids: Phospholipids (e.g., LECITHIN in plasma membranes — glycerol + 2 fatty acids + phosphate + choline); Cholesterol (4-ring steroid lipid without fatty acid!).

sections.heading: Nucleic Acids & NCERT Secondary Metabolites (Table 9.3)
sections.summary: Nucleotides join via 3'-5' phosphodiester bonds to build DNA and RNA polymers carrying genetic information. Plants, fungi, and microbes also synthesise diverse secondary metabolites with ecological and pharmaceutical value.
keyPoints: Nucleoside vs Nucleotide: Nitrogenous base + Pentose sugar (Ribose in RNA, 2'-Deoxyribose in DNA) = Nucleoside (Adenosine, Guanosine, Thymidine, Uridine, Cytidine); Nucleoside + Phosphate = Nucleotide (Adenylic acid, etc.).
Purines (9-membered double ring: Adenine, Guanine) vs Pyrimidines (6-membered single ring: Cytosine, Thymine in DNA, Uracil in RNA).
Watson-Crick B-DNA: Antiparallel strands; pitch = 34 A (3.4 nm) with 10 bp per turn -> distance between adjacent bp = 3.4 A (0.34 nm); turn angle = 36 deg per bp.

Secondary Metabolites (Table 9.3 — high-yield matching!): Pigments (Carotenoids, Anthocyanins); Alkaloids (Morphine, Codeine); Terpenoids (Monoterpenes, Diterpenes); Essential oils (Lemon grass oil); Toxins (Abrin, Ricin); Lectins (Concanavalin A); Drugs (Vinblastin, Curcumin); Polymeric substances (Rubber, Gums, Cellulose).

Primary vs Secondary metabolites: Primary metabolites (amino acids, sugars) have identifiable physiological functions in normal metabolism, whereas secondary metabolites aid ecological defence, pollination, or human pharmaceutical/rubber applications.

sections.heading: Enzymes: Classification, Transition State & Catalytic Speed
sections.summary: Nearly all enzymes are globular tertiary proteins (exceptions: Ribozymes — catalytic RNAs). Enzymes accelerate biological reactions millions of times by stabilising the transition state and lowering Activation Energy without altering net Delta G or equilibrium.
keyPoints: Carbonic Anhydrase benchmark: Uncatalysed CO2 + H2O -> H2CO3 forms ~200 molecules/hour; enzyme-catalysed forms ~600,000 molecules/SECOND (accelerates rate ~10 million times!).
Thermostable enzymes: Taq polymerase & enzymes from hot-spring thermophilic organisms retain catalytic activity even at 80-90 deg C!

Catalytic cycle: E + S <-> ES (transient) -> EP -> E + P; Enzymes lower Activation Energy (Ea) barrier between substrate S and Transition State, leaving Delta G (energy difference between S and P) completely UNCHANGED.

6 IUBMB Enzyme Classes (EC 1 to EC 6): (1) Oxidoreductases / Dehydrogenases (redox: S_red + S'_ox -> S_ox + S'_red), (2) Transferases (transfer group G other than H: S-G + S' -> S + S'-G), (3) Hydrolases (hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic, C-C, C-halide, P-N bonds), (4) Lyases (non-hydrolytic group removal leaving DOUBLE BONDS!), (5) Isomerases (interconversion of optical, geometric, positional isomers), (6) Ligases (link 2 compounds coupled to ATP cleavage: C-O, C-S, C-N, P-O).

Inorganic catalysts vs Enzymes: Inorganic catalysts work efficiently at high temperatures and pressures (e.g., >80-100 deg C), whereas most globular enzymes denature above 40 deg C (except thermophilic archaebacterial enzymes).

sections.heading: Factors Affecting Enzyme Activity, Inhibition & Co-factors
sections.summary: Enzyme velocity depends tightly on temperature, pH, substrate concentration, and inhibitors. Competitive inhibitors mimic substrates to raise apparent Km while leaving Vmax unchanged, and non-protein co-factors complete holoenzyme activity.
keyPoints: Temperature & pH: Bell-shaped optimum curve; low temperature preserves enzymes in temporarily INACTIVE state, whereas high temperature DENATURES tertiary protein structure irreversibly.

Substrate Concentration [S]: Hyperbolic saturation curve rising to plateau V_max (all active sites saturated); Michaelis constant K_m = substrate concentration at which reaction velocity equals V_max / 2 (lower K_m = higher substrate affinity!).

Competitive Inhibition (e.g., Malonate closely resembles Succinate inhibiting Succinate Dehydrogenase; Sulpha drugs inhibiting bacterial folate synthesis): Inhibitor competes for ACTIVE SITE -> V_max stays UNCHANGED (high [S] outcompetes inhibitor), while apparent K_m INCREASES!
Holoenzyme = Apoenzyme (protein part, catalytically inactive alone) + Co-factor (non-protein part; removal destroys catalytic activity!).

3 Co-factor Types: (1) Prosthetic groups (organic, TIGHTLY bound to apoenzyme: HAEM in Peroxidase & Catalase breaking H2O2 -> H2O + O2), (2) Co-enzymes (organic, TRANSIENT association during catalysis, often derived from vitamins: NAD & NADP contain Niacin/Vit B3), (3) Metal ions (form coordination bonds at active site & substrate: Zn^2+ for Carboxypeptidase & Carbonic anhydrase!).

sections.heading: Human Respiratory System & Mechanics of Breathing
sections.summary: The human respiratory tract divides into a Conducting Zone (external nostrils to terminal bronchioles — humidifies, warms, clears dust) and an Exchange Zone (alveoli and alveolar ducts). Pulmonary ventilation operates via negative pressure gradients generated by the diaphragm and intercostal muscles.
keyPoints: Conducting pathway: External nostrils -> Nasal chamber -> Pharynx -> Larynx (cartilaginous sound box; Epiglottis elastic cartilaginous flap prevents food entry into glottis) -> Trachea (divides at 5th thoracic vertebra T5 into left & right primary bronchi) -> Secondary/Tertiary bronchi -> Initial & Terminal bronchioles (supported by incomplete cartilaginous rings up to initial bronchioles!).

Lungs & Pleura: Covered by double-layered PLEURA filled with pleural fluid reducing friction; Outer parietal pleura touches thoracic lining, inner visceral pleura contacts lung surface; Anatomical thoracic chamber is airtight (dorsally vertebral column, ventrally sternum, laterally ribs, lower dome-shaped diaphragm).

Inspiration (ACTIVE process): Contraction of DIAPHRAGM (increases thoracic volume in antero-posterior axis) + EXTERNAL INTERCOSTAL muscles (lift ribs & sternum, increasing volume in dorso-ventral axis) -> intrapulmonary pressure falls BELOW atmospheric pressure -> air rushes in.
Normal Expiration (PASSIVE process): Relaxation of diaphragm and external intercostals returns thoracic volume -> intrapulmonary pressure rises slightly ABOVE atmospheric -> air expelled.

Forceful Expiration & Abdominal Breathing: Uses INTERNAL INTERCOSTAL muscles + ABDOMINAL muscles to forcefully compress thoracic cavity; Healthy adult breathes 12-16 times/minute measured by Spirometer.

sections.heading: Respiratory Volumes, Capacities & Alveolar Gas Exchange
sections.summary: Spirometry measures four primary lung volumes and five derived capacities to assess pulmonary function, excluding Residual Volume. Gases diffuse passively across the sub-millimetre three-layer alveolar membrane down partial pressure gradients.
keyPoints: 4 Primary Volumes: Tidal Volume (TV = 500 mL; ~6,000-8,000 mL/min minute ventilation), Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV = 2,500-3,000 mL), Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV = 1,000-1,100 mL), Residual Volume (RV = 1,100-1,200 mL — CANNOT be measured by simple spirometer!).

5 Respiratory Capacities: IC = TV + IRV (~3,000-3,500 mL); EC = TV + ERV (~1,500-1,600 mL); FRC = ERV + RV (~2,100-2,300 mL); VC = ERV + TV + IRV (~4,000-4,600 mL); TLC = RV + ERV + TV + IRV = VC + RV (~5,100-5,800 mL).

Partial Pressures (mm Hg) Table 17.1: Atmospheric Air (pO2 159, pCO2 0.3) -> Alveoli (pO2 104, pCO2 40) -> Deoxygenated Blood (pO2 40, pCO2 45) -> Oxygenated Blood (pO2 95, pCO2 40) -> Tissues (pO2 40, pCO2 45).
Diffusion factors: Partial pressure gradient, Gas solubility (CO2 is 20-25 times MORE soluble than O2, diffusing far faster for identical delta P!), and Membrane thickness.
Alveolar Diffusion Membrane (total thickness < 1 mm): 3 layers — (1) Thin squamous epithelium of alveoli, (2) Endothelium of alveolar capillaries, (3) Fused basement substance in between.

sections.heading: O2 & CO2 Transport, Bohr/Haldane Effects & Respiratory Regulation
sections.summary: Haemoglobin binds four O2 molecules cooperatively to yield a sigmoid dissociation curve sensitive to CO2, pH, and temperature (Bohr shift). CO2 travels predominantly as plasma bicarbonate via RBC carbonic anhydrase and the chloride shift.
keyPoints: O2 Transport: 97% bound reversibly to Haemoglobin (oxyhaemoglobin, Fe2+ haem; 100 mL oxygenated blood delivers ~5 mL O2 to tissues under normal conditions, ~15 mL during strenuous exercise!) + 3% dissolved in plasma.

Oxyhaemoglobin Dissociation Curve (Sigmoid): Left Shift (higher O2 affinity / association at ALVEOLI): High pO2, Low pCO2, Low H+ (high pH), Low Temp, Fetal Hb. Right Shift (BOHR EFFECT — lower affinity / O2 dissociation at TISSUES): Low pO2, High pCO2, High H+ (low pH), High Temp.
CO2 Transport: 70% as Bicarbonate (HCO3-), 20-25% as Carbaminohaemoglobin (bound to amino groups of globin), ~7% dissolved in plasma. Every 100 mL deoxygenated blood delivers ~4 mL CO2 to alveoli!

Carbonic Anhydrase & Chloride Shift (Hamburger phenomenon): Inside RBCs (rich in Carbonic Anhydrase), CO2 + H2O <-> H2CO3 <-> H+ + HCO3-; HCO3- diffuses out into plasma in exchange for Cl- moving INTO RBCs to maintain electrical neutrality.

Neural & Chemical Regulation: Medulla oblongata houses Respiratory Rhythm Centre (primary); Pons houses PNEUMOTAXIC CENTRE (moderates rhythm by shortening inspiration duration!); Chemosensitive area adjacent to rhythm centre + Aortic arch & Carotid artery chemoreceptors are highly sensitive to CO2 and H+ (O2 plays an INSIGNIFICANT role in normal respiratory rhythm!).

Respiratory Disorders: Asthma (bronchi/bronchiole inflammation -> wheezing), Emphysema (chronic cigarette-smoking damage to alveolar walls -> decreased respiratory surface!), Occupational Respiratory Disorders (silicosis/asbestosis -> fibrous proliferation / fibrosis).

sections.heading: Blood Plasma, Formed Elements, ABO/Rh Grouping & Coagulation
sections.summary: Blood consists of 55% straw-coloured plasma and 45% formed elements (RBCs, WBCs, platelets). Surface antigens govern ABO/Rh transfusion compatibility, while injury triggers an enzymatic Ca2+-dependent coagulation cascade.
keyPoints: Plasma (55%): 90-92% water + 6-8% proteins — Fibrinogen (clotting), Globulins (defence/antibodies), Albumins (osmotic balance); Serum = Plasma minus Clotting Factors!

Erythrocytes / RBCs (5-5.5 million/mm3; 12-16 g Hb/100 mL; enucleated biconcave, 120-day lifespan, destroyed in Spleen 'graveyard of RBCs') & Platelets / Thrombocytes (1.5-3.5 lakh/mm3, cell fragments of bone marrow MEGAKARYOCYTES).

Leucocytes / WBCs (6,000-8,000/mm3): Granulocytes = Neutrophils (60-65%, phagocytic), Eosinophils (2-3%, resist infections & allergic reactions!), Basophils (0.5-1%, LEAST abundant, secrete histamine/serotonin/heparin -> inflammatory reactions); Agranulocytes = Lymphocytes (20-25%, B & T immune response) & Monocytes (6-8%, phagocytic macrophages).

ABO Grouping (Karl Landsteiner): Surface Antigens A/B on RBCs vs Plasma Antibodies anti-B/anti-A -> Group O (universal donor: no RBC antigens, has anti-A & anti-B); Group AB (universal recipient: A & B antigens, NO antibodies).

Rh Grouping (~80% humans Rh+): Erythroblastosis foetalis occurs when Rh-NEGATIVE mother conceives an Rh-POSITIVE foetus in her SECOND (or subsequent) pregnancy — maternal anti-Rh IgG antibodies cross placenta causing severe foetal anaemia & jaundice; prevented by injecting anti-Rh antibodies (RhoGAM) to mother immediately after first Rh+ delivery!

Coagulation Cascade: Injured tissue / platelets release Thromboplastin -> activates THROMBOKINASE enzyme complex -> converts inactive Prothrombin --(Ca2+ + Thrombokinase)--> active Thrombin -> converts soluble Fibrinogen -> insoluble Fibrin polymer threads trapping dead/damaged blood cells into a clot!

sections.heading: Human Heart, Myogenic Conduction & 0.8s Cardiac Cycle
sections.summary: The mesodermally derived human heart beats autonomously via nodal tissue without external neural input, executing complete double circulation across pulmonary and systemic circuits. Each 0.8-second cardiac cycle coordinates atrial systole, ventricular systole, and joint diastole.
keyPoints: Heart Valves & Septa: Right atrium-ventricle = TRICUSPID valve (3 muscular flaps); Left atrium-ventricle = BICUSPID / MITRAL valve; Pulmonary artery & Aorta exits = SEMILUNAR valves; Chordae tendineae + papillary muscles prevent AV valve inversion.

Myogenic Nodal Tissue: Sino-Atrial Node (SAN, right upper corner of right atrium — PACEMAKER generating 70-75 action potentials/min) -> Atrio-Ventricular Node (AVN, lower left corner of right atrium near septum) -> AV Bundle (Bundle of His) -> Left & Right Bundle Branches -> Purkinje Fibres through ventricular musculature.

Cardiac Cycle (72 beats/min -> 60/72 = 0.8 seconds/cycle): (1) Joint Diastole (all 4 chambers relaxed, AV valves OPEN, 70% ventricular passive filling!), (2) Atrial Systole (0.1 s: SAN fires, pumps remaining 30% blood into ventricles), (3) Ventricular Systole (0.3 s: AV valves close -> 1st sound LUB; Semilunar valves open pumping blood into aorta/pulmonary trunk), (4) Ventricular Diastole (0.5 s total; Semilunar valves close -> 2nd sound DUB).

Stroke Volume & Cardiac Output: Stroke Volume (blood pumped by EACH ventricle per beat) = ~70 mL; End-Diastolic Volume (EDV ~120 mL) minus End-Systolic Volume (ESV ~50 mL) = SV (70 mL); Cardiac Output = SV x Heart Rate = 70 mL x 72/min = ~5,040 mL/min (~5 L/min).

Double Circulation & Portals: Pulmonary (RV -> Pulmonary artery -> Lungs -> Pulmonary veins -> LA) + Systemic (LV -> Aorta -> Tissues -> Venae cavae -> RA); Hepatic Portal Vein carries nutrient-rich blood from intestine to liver BEFORE systemic return; Coronary system nourishes myocardium; Lymphatic system returns interstitial fluid + absorbed fats (lacteals) to subclavian veins.

sections.heading: Electrocardiograph (ECG), Cardiac Regulation & Circulatory Disorders
sections.summary: An ECG records electrical potentials generated during cardiac depolarisation and repolarisation across standard limb leads (wrists and left ankle). Sympathetic nerves and adrenal hormones boost cardiac output, while vascular pathology underlies hypertension, CAD, angina, and myocardial infarction.
keyPoints: ECG Waves (P-QRS-T): P-wave = electrical excitation / DEPOLARISATION of atria (leads to contraction of both atria); QRS complex = DEPOLARISATION of ventricles (initiates ventricular systole; counting QRS complexes in a given time determines HEART RATE!); T-wave = REPOLARISATION (return from excited to normal state) of ventricles -> end of T-wave marks end of systole!

Neural & Hormonal Regulation: Medulla oblongata cardiac centre modulates heart via ANS — Sympathetic nerves (Noradrenaline) INCREASE heart rate, ventricular contraction strength & cardiac output; Parasympathetic nerves (Vagus / Acetylcholine) DECREASE heart rate, conduction speed & cardiac output; Adrenal medullary hormones increase cardiac output.
Hypertension: Persistent blood pressure >= 140/90 mm Hg (normal = 120 systolic / 80 diastolic mm Hg); damages heart, brain, and kidneys.
Coronary Artery Disease (CAD / Atherosclerosis): Deposition of calcium, fat, cholesterol, and fibrous tissue narrows coronary artery lumen supplying heart muscle.
Angina (Angina pectoris): Acute chest pain caused when insufficient oxygen reaches heart muscle (common in middle-aged/elderly).

Heart Failure vs Cardiac Arrest vs Heart Attack: Heart Failure = heart does NOT pump blood effectively enough to meet body needs (often called Congestive Heart Failure due to lung congestion); Cardiac Arrest = heart STOPS beating; Heart Attack (Myocardial Infarction) = heart muscle is suddenly damaged by inadequate blood supply!

solvedExamples.question: Identify the anatomical site and exact mechanism of the Pneumotaxic Centre in human breathing regulation.
steps: Primary Respiratory Rhythm Centre resides in the Medulla Oblongata.
Pneumotaxic Centre resides in the PONS region of the brain.
Neural signals from the pneumotaxic centre REDUCE the duration of inspiration and thereby alter respiratory rate.
solvedExamples.answer: Located in Pons; reduces duration of inspiration to moderate respiratory rhythm
solvedExamples.pitfall: Placing the pneumotaxic centre in the medulla or thinking it prolongs inspiration.

solvedExamples.question: Assertion (A): First heart sound 'Lub' is associated with closure of tricuspid and bicuspid valves. Reason (R): Ventricular systole raises ventricular pressure above atrial pressure, forcing AV valves shut.
steps: At the start of ventricular systole, rising intraventricular pressure snaps the tricuspid & bicuspid (AV) valves closed -> produces first heart sound 'LUB'.
Both (A) and (R) are completely true statements.
(R) provides the exact physiological mechanism explaining (A).
solvedExamples.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
solvedExamples.pitfall: Mixing up 'Lub' (AV valve closure at start of ventricular systole) with 'Dub' (semilunar valve closure at start of ventricular diastole).

solvedExamples.question: An athlete has Heart Rate = 60 beats/min, End-Diastolic Volume (EDV) = 150 mL, and End-Systolic Volume (ESV) = 50 mL. Calculate (a) Cardiac Cycle duration, (b) Stroke Volume, and (c) Cardiac Output. Also calculate Total Lung Capacity if VC = 4500 mL and FRC = 2200 mL while ERV = 1000 mL.
steps: Cardiac Cycle duration = 60 s / 60 bpm = 1.0 second.
Stroke Volume (SV) = EDV - ESV = 150 - 50 = 100 mL.
Cardiac Output (CO) = SV x HR = 100 mL x 60/min = 6,000 mL/min (6 L/min).
For lung capacity: RV = FRC - ERV = 2200 - 1000 = 1200 mL -> TLC = VC + RV = 4500 + 1200 = 5700 mL.
solvedExamples.answer: Cycle = 1.0 s, SV = 100 mL, CO = 6 L/min | RV = 1200 mL, TLC = 5700 mL
solvedExamples.pitfall: Adding FRC + VC directly (which double-counts ERV = 1000 mL!). Always isolate RV = FRC - ERV first.

solvedExamples.question: Match ECG deflections & Respiratory curve shifts: (1) Ventricular repolarisation, (2) Atrial depolarisation, (3) Rightward shift of O2-Hb curve, (4) Leftward shift of O2-Hb curve.
steps: (1) Ventricular repolarisation = T-wave (marks end of systole).
(2) Atrial depolarisation = P-wave.
(3) Rightward shift (tissue unloading / Bohr effect) = High pCO2, High H+, High temp, Low pO2.
(4) Leftward shift (alveolar loading) = High pO2, Low pCO2, Low H+, Low temp (also Fetal Hb).

sections.heading: Excretion, Nephron Urine Formation & Counter-Current Mechanism
sections.summary: Humans are ureotelic (hepatic ornithine cycle converts toxic NH3 to urea), eliminating wastes via ~1 million nephrons per kidney. Juxtamedullary nephrons (long Henle loops dipping deep into medulla + vasa recta) build a steep 300 to 1200 mOsmol/L gradient enabling ~4x urine concentration.
keyPoints: Nitrogenous wastes: Ammonotelic (most toxic, high water: bony fishes, aquatic amphibians, aquatic insects), Ureotelic (mammals, terrestrial amphibians, marine fishes), Uricotelic (least toxic pellet/paste, minimal water: reptiles, birds, land snails, insects).

Glomerular Filtration (non-selective ultrafiltration through 3 layers: capillary endothelium + podocyte slit pores of Bowman's capsule + basement membrane): Net Filtration Pressure ~10 mm Hg yields GFR = 125 mL/min = 180 Litres/day (99% reabsorbed -> ~1-1.5 L urine/day!).

Tubular Segments: PCT (simple cuboidal brush-border epithelium — reabsorbs 70-80% electrolytes/water + 100% glucose/amino acids + secretes H+, NH3, K+); Descending Henle (permeable to WATER, impermeable to electrolytes -> filtrate concentrates); Ascending Henle (impermeable to water; thin passive NaCl, thick ACTIVE NaCl transport -> filtrate dilutes); DCT (conditional Na+ & water reabsorption + K+/H+ secretion); Collecting Duct (ADH water reabsorption + urea recycling to medullary interstitium).

Counter-Current Multiplier & Exchanger: Opposite flow in two limbs of Henle's loop & Vasa Recta amplifies medullary osmolarity from 300 mOsmol/L (cortex) to 1200 mOsmol/L (inner medulla) using NaCl (Henle ascending -> Vasa recta) and Urea (Collecting duct -> Henle thin ascending).

Hormonal Regulation & Micturition: ADH/Vasopressin (hypothalamus -> posterior pituitary; prevents diuresis via aquaporins + constricts blood vessels); RAAS (Low GFR -> JGA cells release RENIN -> Angiotensinogen -> Ang I -> Ang II [potent vasoconstrictor + stimulates Adrenal Cortex ALDOSTERONE for Na+/water reabsorption at DCT!]); ANF (heart atria -> VASODILATOR opposing RAAS!).

Disorders: Uremia (urea buildup -> artificial kidney Hemodialysis using cellophane tube + heparin/anti-heparin), Renal calculi (oxalate kidney stones), Glomerulonephritis (glomeruli inflammation); Sweat (NaCl, urea, lactic acid) & Sebum (sterols, hydrocarbons, waxes) aid excretion.

sections.heading: Locomotion, Sarcomere Ultrastructure & Human Skeletal System
sections.summary: Cells exhibit amoeboid (macrophages/leucocytes), ciliary (trachea/oviduct), and muscular movements. Skeletal muscle contraction obeys Huxley's Sliding Filament Theory where thin actin filaments slide over stationary thick myosin filaments inside each sarcomere.
keyPoints: Muscle fibre organisation: Fascicles held by fascia -> Sarcolemma encloses sarcoplasm + Sarcoplasmic Reticulum (Ca2+ storehouse!) + parallel myofibrils showing alternating light I-band (isotropic, Actin ONLY, bisected by Z-line) and dark A-band (anisotropic, Myosin + overlapping Actin, central pale H-zone bisected by M-line). Functional unit = SARCOMERE (Z-line to Z-line).

Contractile Proteins: Thin filament = 2 helically wound F-Actin polymers (G-actin monomers) + 2 Tropomyosin filaments + Troponin (3 subunits: TpI masks myosin-binding site on actin, TpC binds Ca2+, TpT binds tropomyosin). Thick filament = polymerised Meromyosins (HMM globular head with ATPase & actin-binding sites + short arm -> cross-arm; LMM tail).

Sliding Filament Mechanism: Motor neuron releases Acetylcholine -> sarcolemma action potential -> SR releases Ca2+ -> Ca2+ binds Troponin -> unmasks active sites on Actin -> Myosin head hydrolyses ATP forming cross-bridge, pulling Actin inward -> I-band & H-zone SHORTEN/disappear while A-BAND STAYS CONSTANT LENGTH! New ATP binding breaks cross-bridge for relaxation.

Red vs White Muscle Fibres: Red (high Myoglobin, abundant mitochondria, aerobic, sustained contraction) vs White (low myoglobin, few mitochondria, abundant sarcoplasmic reticulum, anaerobic lactic acid fatigue).

206 Human Bones: Axial (80 = Skull 29 [Cranial 8, Facial 14, Ear ossicles 6 Malleus/Incus/Stapes, Hyoid 1 U-shaped] + Vertebral column 26 [C7-T12-L5-S1fused-C1fused] + Sternum 1 + Ribs 12 pairs [1-7 True vertebrosternal, 8-10 False vertebrochondral, 11-12 Floating!]) + Appendicular (126 = Pectoral girdle 4 [2 Clavicle + 2 Scapula acromion/glenoid], Pelvic girdle 2 coxal bones [Ilium+Ischium+Pubis -> Acetabulum + Pubic symphysis fibrous cartilage], 2x30 Forelimbs + 2x30 Hindlimbs + Patella sesamoid!).

Joints & Disorders: Fibrous (skull sutures — immovable), Cartilaginous (intervertebral discs, pubic symphysis — limited movement), Synovial (fluid cavity — Ball & socket shoulder/hip, Hinge knee/elbow, Pivot atlas-axis, Gliding carpals, Saddle carpal-metacarpal thumb!). Disorders: Myasthenia gravis (autoimmune ACh receptor block -> paralysis), Muscular dystrophy (genetic progressive degeneration), Tetany (low Ca2+ wild spasms), Arthritis, Osteoporosis (low estrogen postmenopausal bone mass drop), Gout (uric acid crystal accumulation).

sections.heading: Neural Control: Neuron, Action Potential, Synapse & Human Brain
sections.summary: Neurons generate and propagate electrical action potentials along polarised axolemma using voltage-gated Na+ and K+ channels. Signal transmission across chemical synapses relies on Ca2+-mediated neurotransmitter release, integrating in the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain.
keyPoints: Neuron types: Multipolar (cerebral cortex — 1 axon, 2+ dendrites), Bipolar (retina — 1 axon, 1 dendrite), Unipolar (embryonic stage — 1 axon only). Schwann cells form myelin sheath in PNS leaving unmyelinated Nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction); Oligodendrocytes myelinate CNS!

Resting Membrane Potential (-70 mV, polarised: outside +, inside -): Axoplasm has high K+ & negatively charged proteins, low Na+; maintained by active Na+/K+ ATPase pump transporting 3 Na+ OUTWARDS for 2 K+ INWARDS, plus higher resting permeability to K+ than Na+.

Action Potential: Threshold stimulus opens voltage-gated Na+ channels -> rapid Na+ INFLUX -> DEPOLARISATION (+30 to +45 mV reversal) -> rapid Na+ inactivation & voltage-gated K+ channels open -> K+ EFFLUX -> REPOLARISATION (brief hyperpolarisation) -> Na+/K+ pump restores gradient.

Electrical vs Chemical Synapse: Electrical (rare, pre/post membranes very close via gap junctions -> faster direct current flow) vs Chemical (20 nm synaptic cleft; impulse triggers voltage-gated Ca2+ influx -> synaptic vesicles fuse & release neurotransmitters like Acetylcholine -> bind post-synaptic ligand-gated receptors generating EPSP or IPSP).

Forebrain: Cerebrum (left & right hemispheres joined by CORPUS CALLOSUM nerve tract; grey matter cortex outer cell bodies vs white matter myelinated inner tracts; sensory, motor & association areas for memory/communication), Thalamus (major sensory-motor relay centre), Hypothalamus (thermoregulation, hunger, thirst, circadian, neurosecretory pituitary hormones), Limbic System (Amygdala + Hippocampus + inner cerebral lobes — sexual behaviour, emotional excitement/rage/fear, motivation).

Midbrain & Hindbrain: Midbrain (between thalamus & pons; Cerebral Aqueduct; 4 dorsal round swellings CORPORA QUADRIGEMINA); Hindbrain (Pons fibre tracts + Cerebellum convoluted cortex for posture/balance/precision + Medulla Oblongata regulating respiration, cardiovascular reflexes, gastric secretions); Brainstem = Midbrain + Pons + Medulla!

sections.heading: Endocrine System I: Hypothalamus, Pituitary, Pineal, Thyroid & Parathyroid
sections.summary: Endocrine glands secrete trace non-nutrient chemical messengers (hormones) directly into blood. The hypothalamus orchestrates adenohypophysis via portal vessels and directly supplies neurohypophysis axons, governing growth, metabolism, circadian rhythms, and calcium homeostasis.
keyPoints: Hypothalamus & Pituitary (in Sella turcica bony cavity of sphenoid): Hypothalamic releasing/inhibiting hormones (GnRH, Somatostatin) travel via HYPOPHYSEAL PORTAL SYSTEM to Anterior Pituitary (Pars distalis).

Anterior Pituitary (6 hormones): GH (excess in children = Gigantism, excess in adults = Acromegaly gorilla-like face, deficiency = Pituitary dwarfism), PRL (milk synthesis & mammary growth), TSH, ACTH, LH & FSH (Gonadotropins — males: LH stimulates Leydig androgens, FSH + androgens stimulate Sertoli spermatogenesis; females: LH triggers ovulation & corpus luteum, FSH develops ovarian follicles). Pars intermedia secretes MSH (melanin pigmentation).

Posterior Pituitary (Pars nervosa / Neurohypophysis): Does NOT synthesise hormones — stores & releases hypothalamic OXYTOCIN (smooth muscle contraction: uterine childbirth contractions + milk EJECTION!) and VASOPRESSIN / ADH (distal renal water/electrolyte reabsorption; deficiency causes DIABETES INSIPIDUS with dilute polyuria & polydipsia!).
Pineal Gland (dorsal forebrain): Secretes MELATONIN (24-hour diurnal sleep-wake cycle, body temp, metabolism, pigmentation, menstrual cycle & defence).

Thyroid Gland (2 lobes joined by isthmus): Follicular cells use IODINE to make T4 (Thyroxine) & T3 -> regulate BMR, RBC formation, carb/protein/fat metabolism, water-electrolyte balance. Hypothyroidism (simple goitre from I2 deficiency; pregnancy Cretinism -> stunted mental/physical growth, deaf-mutism!) vs Hyperthyroidism (Exophthalmic Goitre / Graves' disease -> enlarged thyroid, protruding eyeballs, high BMR, weight loss!). Parafollicular C-cells secrete THYROCALCITONIN (TCT — hypocalcaemic, lowers blood Ca2+!).

Parathyroid Gland (4 glands on dorsal thyroid): Secretes peptide PARATHYROID HORMONE (PTH — HYPERCALCAEMIC hormone antagonising TCT: stimulates bone resorption/demineralisation, renal Ca2+ reabsorption, gut Ca2+ absorption!).

sections.heading: Endocrine System II: Thymus, Adrenal, Pancreas, Gonads & Hormone Mechanisms
sections.summary: Thymus matures T-lymphocyte immunity, Adrenal glands balance electrolytes, stress cortisol, and emergency catecholamines, and Pancreatic Islets of Langerhans tightly regulate blood glucose. Peptide hormones act via cell-surface second messengers, whereas steroid and thyroid hormones directly regulate nuclear gene transcription.
keyPoints: Thymus (lobular gland between lungs behind sternum): Secretes peptide THYMOSINS promoting T-lymphocyte differentiation (cell-mediated immunity) & antibody production; degenerates with age -> weak immunity in elderly.

Adrenal Cortex (3 layers outside-in — GFR): Zona Glomerulosa (Mineralocorticoids: ALDOSTERONE raises Na+/water reabsorption & K+/phosphate excretion at DCT), Zona Fasciculata (Glucocorticoids: CORTISOL stimulates gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, proteolysis, anti-inflammatory & suppresses immunity!), Zona Reticularis (androgenic steroids). Hyposecretion of adrenal cortex -> ADDISON'S DISEASE (altered carb metabolism, acute weakness, fatigue).

Adrenal Medulla: Secretes Catecholamines — Adrenaline (Epinephrine) & Noradrenaline (Norepinephrine) ('3F Fight-or-Flight' emergency hormones: alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection, sweating, tachycardia, elevated respiration, glycogenolysis -> glucose!).

Pancreas (composite exocrine + 1-2% Islets of Langerhans endocrine): Alpha-cells secrete GLUCAGON (peptide, HYPERGLYCAEMIC: hepatic glycogenolysis & gluconeogenesis, reduces cellular glucose uptake); Beta-cells secrete INSULIN (peptide, HYPOGLYCAEMIC: enhances hepatocyte/adipocyte glucose uptake & glycogenesis!). Prolonged hyperglycaemia -> DIABETES MELLITUS (glycosuria + ketone bodies -> Insulin therapy!).

Gonads & Organ Hormones: Testis Leydig cells (Testosterone -> spermatogenesis, male secondary traits, anabolic protein/carb effects); Ovary (Estrogen from growing follicles -> female secondary traits, endometrium proliferation; Progesterone from Corpus Luteum -> supports pregnancy & mammary alveoli milk secretion!). Heart ANF (lowers BP); Kidney JGA Erythropoietin (stimulates RBC erythropoiesis!); GI tract Gastrin (HCl/pepsinogen), Secretin (pancreatic H2O/HCO3-), CCK (pancreatic enzymes + gallbladder bile!), GIP (inhibits gastric secretion).

Hormone Action Mechanisms: (1) Water-soluble Peptide/Protein/Catecholamines (Insulin, Glucagon, Pituitary FSH/LH, Epinephrine) bind MEMBRANE-BOUND receptors -> generate 2nd messengers (cAMP, IP3, Ca2+) activating biochemical cascades; (2) Lipid-soluble Steroids (Cortisol, Testosterone, Estradiol, Progesterone) & Iodothyronines (T3/T4) enter cell -> bind INTRACELLULAR/NUCLEAR receptors -> hormone-receptor complex binds DNA regulating gene transcription!

solvedExamples.question: A resting adult kidney filters 180 L of plasma per day (GFR = 125 mL/min) and excretes 1.5 L of urine daily. Calculate (a) % of glomerular filtrate reabsorbed, and (b) net Na+ and K+ ions moved across the axolemma if the Na+/K+ ATPase hydrolyses 100 ATP molecules.
steps: Each ATP hydrolysed pumps 3 Na+ OUT and 2 K+ IN.
For 100 ATP molecules: 300 Na+ ions pumped OUT of axoplasm and 200 K+ ions pumped IN.
solvedExamples.answer: 99.17% (~99%) filtrate reabsorbed; 300 Na+ OUT and 200 K+ IN
solvedExamples.pitfall: Swapping 3 Na+ out / 2 K+ in stoichiometry (writing 2 Na+ / 3 K+).

solvedExamples.question: In a contracting skeletal muscle sarcomere diagram, identify what happens to (P) Z-line distance, (Q) I-band width, (R) H-zone width, and (S) A-band width.
steps: Actin thin filaments slide inward toward the M-line pulling Z-lines closer -> (P) Decreases (sarcomere shortens).
Non-overlapping actin region shrinks -> (Q) I-band shortens.
Central non-overlapping myosin zone shrinks/vanishes -> (R) H-zone shortens/disappears.
Myosin filament length remains unaltered -> (S) A-band stays CONSTANT.
solvedExamples.answer: P decreases, Q decreases, R decreases/disappears, S remains constant
solvedExamples.pitfall: Marking A-band as shortening along with I-band and H-zone.
